title: A three-day kit without unnecessary purchases
h1: A reliable three-day kit without unnecessary purchases
dek: What FEMA and the CDC say a basic kit holds, which items you probably own already, which are worth buying, and how to build it over a few ordinary grocery trips. No products, brands or affiliate links.
description: Build a three-day emergency kit from FEMA, Ready.gov and CDC lists: water, food, light, medicines, documents and cash, with budget tips and honest limits.
recheck: If Ready.gov, FEMA or the CDC revise their kit lists, or at the next quarterly source sweep.

source_use.start-ready-kit: The Basic Disaster Supplies Kit list and additional items; storing items in airtight bags in one or two easy-to-carry containers; maintenance; home, work and car kits.
source_use.start-ready-supply-list: The printable checklist, the 'only a starting point' caveat and the recommendation of one full kit at home plus smaller portable kits elsewhere.
source_use.start-ready-food: Several-day non-perishable food; choose foods your family will eat; example items; the four-hour refrigerator figure and the swollen/dented can rule; outdoor-only cooking appliances.
source_use.ready-are-you-ready: 'At least 72 hours'; water of 3, 7 or 14 days depending on location; cash in small bills; N95 masks; the maintenance steps; bottled water for the kit; learning to shut off utilities before an emergency. Its 2020 'discard refrigerated medication after a day' line, shown as older than the 2023 FEMA sheet.
source_use.cdc-water-store: Water baseline of 1 gallon per person per day for at least 3 days, and try for 2 weeks.
source_use.start-ready-power: Outage effects; refrigerator and freezer holding times; Ready.gov's two-hour food rule and discard-medicine wording (older than FEMA's 2023 sheet); 20-foot generator rule; talk to your provider about how long medicine can be stored warm.
source_use.start-cdc-family-kit: The two-week medication figure; essential-items list; additions for infants and young children; check every six months.
source_use.start-cdc-disability-kit: One week of prescription medication; chargers and batteries for adaptive equipment; check every six months.
source_use.start-redcross-older-adults: At least 30 days of medications and extra assistive items.
source_use.start-ready-disability: 'Several days supply of prescription medicines'; tips for specific disabilities.
source_use.start-cdc-pyh-prescriptions: Talk to a doctor or pharmacist about an emergency supply; keep a medicine list; no number of days given.
source_use.start-ready-low-cost: Garage sales and thrift stores for camping gear, tools and cookware; older clothing that fits.
source_use.start-ready-financial: Small amounts of cash in small bills; document storage.
source_use.start-ready-car: The car kit extras and keeping the tank full.
source_use.start-cdc-infant-checklist: Ready-to-feed formula is the safest formula option; check the kit monthly because babies grow quickly.
source_use.start-fema-power-sheet: FEMA's December 2023 power-outage fact sheet: replace refrigerated medicines after a day or more unless the label says otherwise, call the doctor or pharmacist, use only until a new supply; 4-hour food rule; 20 feet from building openings; no grill, dryer or stove for heat.
